howWeWorkPage.body: Every engagement follows the same four-phase path. The output of each phase is a concrete artifact the team can review, challenge, or approve before the next one starts.
howWeWorkPage.expectHeading: What to expect in each phase
howWeWorkPage.expectIntro: A visible deliverable at every stage, so there are no surprises at handover.
howWeWorkPage.understandBody: Business goal, stack, constraints and success criteria. Output: a short brief and a proposed scope.
howWeWorkPage.designBody: Architecture, scope, risks and milestones. Output: a technical plan with visible checkpoints.
howWeWorkPage.buildBody: Implementation with visible progress. Output: running software, reviewed in short cycles.
howWeWorkPage.handoverBody: Deploy, document and transfer ownership. Output: working system, runbooks and a knowledge transfer session.
howWeWorkPage.deliverablesHeading: What you receive at the end
howWeWorkPage.deliverablesBody: Every engagement ends with a transfer of ownership, not a hand-off to a maintenance contract. The team that receives the work gets the software, the documentation, and the knowledge to operate it.
howWeWorkPage.deliverable1Body: Deployed, tested, and running in your environment. Not a prototype, not a pilot — production-ready code.
howWeWorkPage.deliverable2Body: Architecture decisions, runbooks, deployment steps, and operational notes written for the team that will maintain the system.
howWeWorkPage.deliverable3Body: A structured session with the engineers who will own the system going forward. Questions answered, trade-offs explained, next steps agreed.
howWeWorkPage.principlesBody: These are not values on a poster. They are the constraints we operate within on every engagement.
howWeWorkPage.principle1Body: You speak to the engineer doing the work. No account manager, no project coordinator, no translation layer.
howWeWorkPage.principle2Body: Every two weeks you see working software and a written update. No black boxes, no surprise invoices.
howWeWorkPage.principle3Body: We will tell you if something is outside what we can deliver well. A fixed-price audit is often the right first step when the problem is unclear.
howWeWorkPage.principle4Body: The code, the infrastructure, and the documentation belong to you. We do not build dependencies on our continued involvement.
